questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the university, its location - close to exciting and interesting nature as well as an interest in the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy! I did not have any major issues but it could be a little confusing at times.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a couple of intro meetings and were told where the office dedicated to international students was.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't the easiest, but if you are persistent and look at all the options on Ralphie's list you will definetely find something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't give up!! There is housing to be had, sometimes just very expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty smooth!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the 'courses' part of the website it should be pretty easy to register for courses. If you want upper-level courses you need to write to the instructor. They all responded pretty quickly and I had no major issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I believe there is a guide on the website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into almost all the classes I wanted, except one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write to the instructors!! They are usually nice and helpful about getting you into their classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The high amount of homework and constant tests as well as required attendance is definitely quite different from how things are done at UCPH, where you are allowed more independence. Upper level courses are about as difficult as they are in UCPH but sometimes the academic difficulty level can be a bit lower.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: For the most part all the upper level courses I took were about the same level as they would have been at UCPH, if maybe sometimes a bit lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was not too into the constant tests, midterms and required attendance, but other than that classroom culture is pretty relaxed and you're never afraid to ask questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Principles of Geomorphology
Paleobiology
GIS for Geologists
Geology of Colorado

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Principles of Geomorphology was awesome!!! Katherine is such a great teacher and the material is hugely interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of a sudden tuberculosis test they needed done was about the worst.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eggs are very cheap!! Also i really recommend looking into Buff Pantry where they offer you free leftover food from supermarkets. Otherwise most day-to-day items are about as expensive or maybe a little more expensive than in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The amount of outdoor stuff to do around Boulder is astounding. If you are at all into mountains and nature this should be a huge reason to go.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots and lots of clubs for about every possible niche interest or sport.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The alpine club, if you are into climbing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking!!! Go explore not just Colorado but also all of the other surrounding states. There is so much to see and explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open to taking opportunities when they present themselves. If someone asks you to go with them on a hike, go!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans can sometimes seem a little shallow and over-eager to get to know you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The constant friendlyness!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go outside! Explore! Take other people with you!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seriously look into Buff Pantry.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The human connections as well as getting to live in such a beaitiful place with that many outdoor experiences just around the corner.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It's easy to feel lonely when you are that far away from home. Don't be afraid to just reach out to people, also people you don't know that well - most of them will be eager to get to know you!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I loved my time in Boulder and definetely recommend going.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
